proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOE back no new loans or loan guarantees, seek to sunset its loan authority through Congress and eventually eliminate the Loan Programs Office. If the programs continue, it recommends stronger due diligence and transparency, limiting new lending to grid reliability, resilience and national security projects, and requiring applicants to comply with the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act and to certify they have no other public financing.
remaining: Congress would need to sunset DOE's Title 17 authority; the 2025 reconciliation law instead extended and refunded a modified Section 1706 program, and no sunset bill was identified.
DOE would need to stop issuing new loans and guarantees rather than redirecting them toward reliability and nuclear projects.
The Mandate's applicant conditions (Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act compliance and a no-stacking certification) were not confirmed in the interim final rule or guidance reviewed.

status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) rescinded unobligated IRA loan authority for several Title 17 categories and ended the ATVM program, but also replaced the Section 1706 program with a new Energy Dominance Financing authority backed by new appropriations through 2028. DOE renamed the office (the Loan Programs Office now operates as the Office of Energy Dominance Financing) and has kept closing large loans, including a $26.5 billion Southern Company package (announced 2026-02-25), a loan of up to $1.9 billion for the Duane Arnold restart (2026-09-08) and a conditional commitment of up to $4.2 billion to Vistra (2026-10-05). The shift toward grid reliability, nuclear and critical minerals partly resembles the Mandate's fallback guidance, but its primary recommendation to stop new lending was not followed.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed. Sec. 50402 rescinds unobligated IRA loan commitment authority for several Title 17 categories, the ATVM program is repealed, and Sec. 50403 creates an Energy Dominance Financing authority with new appropriations (about $1 billion through FY2028 per law-firm analysis).
DOE publishes an interim final rule amending 10 CFR Part 609 to implement the new Energy Dominance Financing provisions, broadening eligible project definitions; comments due about 60 days later.
DOE's new organization chart shows the Loan Programs Office as the Office of Energy Dominance Financing, per Latitude Media.

DOE announces a closed $26.5 billion loan package to two Southern Company subsidiaries for generation, nuclear uprates, storage and transmission; the page's metadata date differs from the stated date.

DOE's Office of Energy Dominance Financing issues updated Title 17 guidance emphasizing grid reliability, capacity expansion, supply chains and critical minerals, with narrower greenhouse gas requirements, per Greenberg Traurig.
DOE closes a loan of up to $1.9 billion to NextEra Energy to restart the Duane Arnold nuclear plant in Iowa, pending NRC approvals.
DOE announces a conditional commitment of up to $4.2 billion to Vistra for nuclear uprates in Pennsylvania and Ohio; not yet a funded loan.

title: End new DOE loans and guarantees and sunset the Loan Programs Office
uncertainties: The Mondaq article's date was not shown (July 2025 assumed). The Southern Company announcement page shows conflicting dates (2026-02-25 in the text, 2026-01-25 in metadata). Conflicting estimates of lending capacity were not reconciled. Cancellations of earlier conditional commitments were not verified. The DOE Energy Dominance Financing page (checked 2026-10-13) lists no announcement after 2026-10-05, and states that the Loan Programs Office operates as the Office of Energy Dominance Financing. DOE's FY2027 budget justification for the office (publication date not shown on the page, so not added to the timeline) requests $30 billion of new loan guarantee commitment authority under Title 17 and $200 million of credit subsidy for advanced nuclear, while cancelling about $2.32 billion of unobligated ATVM credit subsidy and earlier Title 17 authority and expecting no new ATVM loans; this continues lending rather than ending it. The House Appropriations Committee approved its FY2027 Energy and Water bill on 2026-05-20, but its treatment of the loan office was not found in the two pages read, and enactment status of FY2026 or FY2027 appropriations for the office was not confirmed.
